body:
## [29.0.0] - 2026-11-15 🛡️ The "Trust the numbers" Release ✅ ~104 commits since 28.0.0, and the theme is **correctness**. We develop qsv with the latest models from Anthropic and review every change adversarially with OpenAI. [Codacy](https://www.codacy.com) adds one more layer of correctness review on top of that. Thanks to their generosity, we now have free access to their platform. With all three, we swept several core commands for correctness: `stats` and `moarstats`, `luau`, `profile`, `scoresql`, `sqlp --format avro`, and every command that reads piped stdin. Thank you, Codacy! - **`validate --sarif` writes JSON Schema errors as a [SARIF 2.1.0](https://www.oasis-open.org/standard/sarif-v2-1-0/) log file** ([#5031](https://github.com/dathere/qsv/pull/5031)). Though SARIF is typically used for static code analysis, we're now using it to report validation errors in a standardized format, with an [example GitHub Actions workflow](https://github.com/dathere/qsv/tree/master/resources/examples/validate-sarif) that uploads them to GitHub code scanning. See the [wiki walk-through](https://github.com/dathere/qsv/wiki/Validation-and-Schema#sarif) and the [sample repo](https://github.com/jqnatividad/qsv-sarif-test) where the workflow raised code scanning alerts, including on a [pull request](https://github.com/jqnatividad/qsv-sarif-test/pull/1).
This sets the stage for integrating qsv's validation capabilities into Datapusher+, CI/CD pipelines and other automated workflows. Beyond validating deterministic JSON Schema errors, the SARIF format will allow us to do **neuro-symbolic, static data validation & analysis** with a model trained on the FAIRified metadata we compile in Verikan[^1]. This was inspired by Codacy's SARIF support. - **`stats` no longer crashes on `NaN` cells** ([#5053](https://github.com/dathere/qsv/pull/5053)). If you run `stats` on data written by pandas or numpy, upgrade. In qsv 28.0.0 and 27.0.1, `stats --median`, `--quartiles` or `--everything` panicked on a float column of a few hundred rows or more that holds a `NaN`, `nan` or `NAN` cell, which is how pandas and numpy write missing values. So did `moarstats`, which runs `stats`. On smaller columns, the `sum` came out empty and the quartiles, MAD, IQR, fences and percentiles were empty or shifted. Every numeric statistic now skips `NaN` cells, as the mean and `--quantile-method approx` already did. A `NaN` cell still counts as a value for `nullcount`, `sparsity` and `cardinality`. Also in this release: - **Piped stdin works in eleven more places.** `sample`, `cat`, `applydp`, `geocode --batch 0`, `input --skip-lastlines`, `partition`, `split --chunks`, `searchset`, `frequency`, `sniff` and `extsort` dropped rows, wrote only the header, or rejected `-` when reading from a pipe, several of them with exit 0 ([#5003](https://github.com/dathere/qsv/pull/5003), [#5005](https://github.com/dathere/qsv/pull/5005), [#5009](https://github.com/dathere/qsv/pull/5009), [#5012](https://github.com/dathere/qsv/pull/5012)). - **Maps render in sandboxed iframes** such as CKAN's Webpage view or the new [ckanext-webpageviewplus](https://github.com/dathere/ckanext-webpageviewplus). Before, every MapLibre map there stayed blank ([#5033](https://github.com/dathere/qsv/pull/5033)). - **The stats cache is no longer served stale** when `QSV_NO_HEADERS`, `QSV_STATS_SEPARATOR` or a sniffed or default delimiter changes, or after an upgrade with `--infer-dates` ([#5049](https://github.com/dathere/qsv/pull/5049), [#5051](https://github.com/dathere/qsv/pull/5051), [#5052](https://github.com/dathere/qsv/pull/5052)). - **`stats --cardinality`, `--mode` and `--everything` are 12–27% faster and use up to 36% less memory**, with and without `--weight` ([#5011](https://github.com/dathere/qsv/pull/5011), [#5013](https://github.com/dathere/qsv/pull/5013)). - **`sqlp` runs on a newer Polars** that adds correlated subqueries, `LATERAL`, `PERCENTILE_CONT`/`PERCENTILE_DISC`, `CREATE VIEW`, `BOOL_AND`, `COUNT_IF`, `MAX_BY`, `REGEXP_EXTRACT` and more. It also fixes two wrong results ([#5055](https://github.com/dathere/qsv/pull/5055) and earlier bumps). - **The MCP server's `.mcpb` bundle is half the size**, 5.6 MB instead of 11.4 MB. The 28.0.0 bundle shipped 119 development-only packages the server never loads, including typescript, c8 and three flagged minimatch copies. They are now left out ([#5014](https://github.com/dathere/qsv/pull/5014)). - **Dependency bumps for security fixes, and bundled-library updates.** - Security: - The SQLite that `to sqlite` bundles is now 3.54.1, which fixes [RUSTSEC-2026-0459](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0459) ([#5022](https://github.com/dathere/qsv/pull/5022)). - The Polars bump moves to zstd 0.14, which clears 13 "unsound" advisories ([#5021](https://github.com/dathere/qsv/pull/5021)). - The MCP server takes `hono` and `@hono/node-server` security releases ([#5042](https://github.com/dathere/qsv/pull/5042), [#5043](https://github.com/dathere/qsv/pull/5043)). - Bundled libraries: - Luau is now 0.745, with native-code (`luau-jit`) crash and code-generation fixes ([#5026](https://github.com/dathere/qsv/pull/5026)). - [driver.js](https://driverjs.com), the engine behind the Data Schematic Tour, is now 1.14.0 (from 1.10.2). Enter now advances every step, and the spotlight follows elements that scroll or re-render ([#5038](https://github.com/dathere/qsv/pull/5038), [#5057](https://github.com/dathere/qsv/pull/5057)). This is a major release because some `sqlp`, `validate`, `profile --strict`, `luau` and `stats` results and exit codes change. See [Breaking Changes](https://github.com/dathere/qsv/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md#v29-breaking-changes). The MSRV is now Rust 1.100. ### ⚡ Performance Measured with qsv's benchmark suite, using the same machine, dataset and build type as 28.0.0: a Mac mini (M2 Pro, 12 cores, 32 GiB), 1M rows × 41 columns of NYC 311 data (520 MB), and the prebuilt PGO binary. Across 305 benchmarks, the median one is 1.2% faster, 69 are more than 5% faster, and 6 are more than 5% slower. Full results are in the [Benchmarks Data Schematic](https://dathere.github.io/qsv/benchmarks/). - **`stats --everything` is 12–28% faster and uses 13–24% less memory** ([#5011](https://github.com/dathere/qsv/pull/5011), [#5013](https://github.com/dathere/qsv/pull/5013)). A full pass over the dataset drops from 2.41 s to 2.02 s, and from 0.55 s to 0.39 s with an index. `stats --cardinality` is 15% faster and uses 20% less memory. Commands that run `stats` internally gain as well: `schema` is 11% faster and `synthesize` 13% faster. Plain `stats` (without `--everything` or `--cardinality`) is about 4% slower: 1.04 s → 1.08 s. - **`searchset` is 11–12% faster, uses half the CPU time, and peaks at 22 MiB instead of ~990 MiB** ([#5012](https://github.com/dathere/qsv/pull/5012)). It no longer counts every row up front unless the progress bar is on. - **`luau` scripts are 9–11% faster** with Luau 0.745 ([#5026](https://github.com/dathere/qsv/pull/5026)). `luau filter` is unchanged. - **`joinp` is 5–12% faster** with the newer Polars ([#5055](https://github.com/dathere/qsv/pull/5055) and earlier bumps). - **`to ods` is 41% faster**, taking 16.2 s instead of 27.6 s. ### 🙏 Contributors Thanks to everyone who made 29.0.0 possible: - [@acdha](https://github.com/acdha) for reporting that `sample` behaved differently on stdin ([#4999](https://github.com/dathere/qsv/issues/4999)). That report led to the stdin fixes across eleven commands. - [@mitsuhiko](https://github.com/mitsuhiko) for adding a bundled time zone database fallback to [MiniJinja](https://github.com/mitsuhiko/minijinja)'s datetime filters at our request ([mitsuhiko/minijinja#1008](https://github.com/mitsuhiko/minijinja/issues/1008)). With it, `template` handles legacy zone names such as `EST`. - [@ik1ne](https://github.com/ik1ne) for merging the zip 9 bump in [`webdriver-downloader`](https://github.com/ik1ne/webdriver-downloader) and releasing it as 0.18.0 ([ik1ne/webdriver-downloader#67](https://github.com/ik1ne/webdriver-downloader/pull/67)), which let qsv drop its fork patch Detailed Changelog: https://github.com/dathere/qsv/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md#v29-changes **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/dathere/qsv/compare/28.0.0...29.0.0 --- [^1]: Verikan is an open-source, neuro-symbolic knowledge harness that provides verified, deterministic, traceable, cryptographically signed answers to natural language questions. It can be connected to ANY data portal that supports the DCAT standard. We've been working on it with our partners in Western PA since last year and it will be released soon!
